audit: The courier analogy separates subject, actor and credential, but readers need to apply the permission intersection to specific orders rather than remember identity terminology. Lesson A varies one permission ceiling at a time across four concrete refund cases; an all-allow row still requires downstream financial and approval checks. Lesson B presents a verified token with the expected refund scope but the wrong audience, demonstrating why apparently strong claims cannot be repurposed. Neither lesson promises that token exchange automatically narrows scopes or makes a token one-use. Background jobs remain outside the explicitly user-directed setup, preserving their separate principal and policy model.

lessons.title: Three permission ceilings must overlap
lessons.intro: Priya asks the refunds workload to act on an order. These constructed cases vary user entitlement, workload authority and the current task scope independently.

data.rule: All three must allow; approval, credential and downstream financial checks still apply.

read: Compare each row with the scoped-refund baseline.
A single denial defeats the intersection even when the other two columns allow.
The first row passes these ceilings, not every execution requirement.
lessons.question: Can the refunds workload compensate for Priya lacking access to O-902?
lessons.answer: No. User-directed authority is constrained by both principals and the task, not the union of their powers. The workload's permission cannot supply the missing user entitlement.
lessons.takeaway: Intersect authority; never combine privileges to bypass a denial.
lessons.assumption: Fictional user-directed cases; background jobs use a separate reviewed workload policy. Other refund conditions are not represented in this matrix.

lessons.title: Right scope, wrong audience
lessons.intro: The executor is about to call payments-api. Its credential is cryptographically valid and current, but was issued for the reporting service. The model never receives the credential.
read: The summary is claim metadata, not a usable bearer token.
Scope presence does not override the intended resource server.
The payments boundary must reject the wrong audience.
lessons.question: Should the executor retry using a broad service token after this denial?
lessons.answer: No. It should resolve the incorrect credential profile through the authorized broker. Any replacement must satisfy the user, workload, task and resource policy; a broader credential is not a recovery shortcut.
lessons.takeaway: Validate destination binding independently of scope.
lessons.assumption: Fictional validated claim summary, not a credential. Exchange policy determines audience and delegation claims; scope does not prove business entitlement.
